title: WM-MT141-SessionWorktreeBranchMode
clause: Session worktrees provision on named session/<id> branches (detach kept as compat mode); keep-until-merged reclaim

scope.summary:
GOAL: Upgrade session worktree provisioning in src/backend/handshake_core/src/workspace_safety.rs from detached-HEAD checkouts to named session branches, so downstream merge-back (MT-142..147) has a real branch to merge, while preserving the existing --detach behavior behind a backward-compat mode. This MT is the foundation of the WM family: today ensure_session_worktree_allocation (~line 370) runs `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true worktree add --detach <worktree_path> HEAD` under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK, placing worktrees under session_worktrees/<session_id> (or HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_ROOT, session_worktree_path ~line 356), and a detached worktree's commits are unreachable refs once the worktree is removed.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: workspace_safety.rs gains a typed checkout-mode enum, a mode-aware allocation function (the existing ensure_session_worktree_allocation becomes a thin wrapper), branch naming/collision policy, and a branch-aware cleanup path. swarm_orchestration/events.rs FR worktree event payloads gain branch/mode fields (NO new event kinds; kinds stay FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CREATED/MOUNTED/RECLAIMED/CLEANUP-FAILED, events.rs lines 75-78). New tests under the handshake_core test tree.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Typed enums (in workspace_safety.rs):
   pub enum SessionWorktreeCheckoutMode { SessionBranch { base_ref: String }, DetachedHead }
   pub enum SessionBranchReclaimPolicy { KeepUntilMerged, DeleteOnReclaim }
   Default mode = SessionBranch; default base_ref resolution order: explicit caller argument > HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_BASE_REF env (trimmed, non-empty) > the repo's current branch (the WP feature branch in governed runs) > literal "HEAD". Default reclaim policy = KeepUntilMerged (the branch survives worktree removal until MT-147 confirms merge).
2. Function signatures:
   pub fn ensure_session_worktree_allocation_with_mode(repo_root: &Path, session_id: &str, mode: SessionWorktreeCheckoutMode) -> io::Result<SessionWorktreeAllocation>
   pub fn ensure_session_worktree_allocation(repo_root: &Path, session_id: &str) -> io::Result<SessionWorktreeAllocation>  // wrapper; resolves default mode
   pub fn cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy(repo_root: &Path, worktree_path: &Path, policy: SessionBranchReclaimPolicy) -> io::Result<()>
   SessionWorktreeAllocation gains fields: branch: Option<String>, checkout_mode (serde-serializable), base_ref: Option<String>.
3. Git command lines (all serialized under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK, all with -c core.longpaths=true, matching the existing invocation shape at workspace_safety.rs ~396-403):
   SessionBranch mode: `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true worktree add -b session/<session_id> <worktree_path> <base_ref>`
   DetachedHead mode (unchanged compat): `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true worktree add --detach <worktree_path> HEAD`
   Branch deletion on DeleteOnReclaim: `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true branch -d session/<session_id>`  // -d NEVER -D: unmerged branches fail closed and surface the error
4. Branch naming policy: branch = "session/" + session_id, validated with `git check-ref-format --branch session/<session_id>` before use; invalid session ids are an error, never silently mangled. Collision handling: if refs/heads/session/<session_id> already exists and is not checked out in any worktree (`git worktree list --porcelain` scan), allocate deterministic suffix session/<session_id>-r2, -r3, ... bounded at -r99, then error. NEVER pass -f/--force to `worktree add` or `branch`; NEVER delete an existing branch to make room.
5. FR events: extend the payloads emitted with FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CREATED and FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED to carry { branch, checkout_mode, base_ref, reclaim_policy } so merge-back tooling and TraceProjection can reconstruct provisioning without git access. No schema re-open of event kinds.
6. BOUNDARY: this MT governs git worktree CODE provisioning only. It is strictly separate from CRDT document merging (kernel/crdt live shared documents). Nothing in this MT may route document state through git or git state through the CRDT layer.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read workspace_safety.rs lines 330-450 (session_worktree_path, ensure_session_worktree_allocation, cleanup_session_worktree, SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK usage) and the existing SessionWorktreeAllocation struct.
2. Add SessionWorktreeCheckoutMode + SessionBranchReclaimPolicy enums and the base_ref resolution helper.
3. Implement ensure_session_worktree_allocation_with_mode with the -b command line, branch validation, and collision suffixing; keep the existing pre-existing-path removal behavior.
4. Convert ensure_session_worktree_allocation into the default-mode wrapper; add a compat entry point (env HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_DETACH=1 forces DetachedHead) so existing callers keep working unchanged.
5. Implement cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy; existing cleanup_session_worktree delegates with KeepUntilMerged.
6. Extend the FR worktree event payload construction sites with the new fields.
7. Write tests (scratch git repo in a temp dir): branch mode creates session/<id> at base_ref; detach compat unchanged; collision produces -r2; branch -d fails closed on unmerged branch under DeleteOnReclaim; KeepUntilMerged leaves the branch after worktree removal; concurrent allocations serialize under the lock.
8. Run proof targets; record measured output.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (GUI IPC allowed only on the GUI MT, MT-146)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/** (CRDT document merging is a separate domain; do not conflate with git worktree code merge)
acceptance_criteria: SessionWorktreeCheckoutMode { SessionBranch{base_ref}, DetachedHead } and SessionBranchReclaimPolicy { KeepUntilMerged, DeleteOnReclaim } exist and are serde-serializable.

ensure_session_worktree_allocation_with_mode provisions `git worktree add -b session/<session_id> <path> <base_ref>` with -c core.longpaths=true under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK; default mode is SessionBranch.
DetachedHead compat mode reproduces the exact pre-MT command shape (`worktree add --detach <path> HEAD`) and is selectable via HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_DETACH=1.
Branch collision yields deterministic session/<id>-rN suffixing (bounded at r99) with no -f/--force and no branch deletion.
Branch deletion path uses `git branch -d` only; a live test proves deleting an unmerged session branch fails closed with a surfaced error.
KeepUntilMerged (default) leaves refs/heads/session/<id> intact after cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy removes the worktree.
FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CREATED / -RECLAIMED payloads carry branch, checkout_mode, base_ref, reclaim_policy; no new FR kinds added.
Zero occurrences of `--force` or `-D` in the branch-management code added by this MT (worktree remove --force is pre-existing cleanup code, untouched).
All git invocations added by this MT include -c core.longpaths=true and run under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK.
expected_tests: scratch-repo test: branch-mode allocation creates worktree AND refs/heads/session/<id> at the requested base_ref
scratch-repo test: detach compat mode leaves no session branch (HEAD detached)
scratch-repo test: second allocation for a colliding branch name yields session/<id>-r2
scratch-repo test: DeleteOnReclaim on an unmerged branch errors (branch -d fails closed), branch still exists
scratch-repo test: KeepUntilMerged leaves the branch after worktree removal
concurrency test: two threads allocating different sessions serialize without git lock errors
implementation_notes: Windows discipline is non-negotiable: every new git Command must chain .args(["-c","core.longpaths=true"]) exactly like the existing call sites (workspace_safety.rs ~383, ~399, ~425) and take the SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK guard first.
Backward-compat is load-bearing: MT-144 (patch fallback) exists precisely because legacy detached worktrees have no branch; do not remove or break the detach path.
The base_ref default 'repo current branch' is read via `git -C <repo_root> branch --show-current`; empty output (detached repo HEAD) falls through to literal HEAD.
Do NOT emit new FR event kinds here; merge-lifecycle kinds (proposed/approved/executed/conflicted/aborted) belong to MT-161 (cross-family seam) and are consumed in MT-145.

Keep the pre-existing stale-worktree removal (`worktree remove --force` on an already-existing path) as-is; that force flag predates this MT and applies to worktree files, never to branches and never to push.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend worktree-provisioning MT; the operator-facing merge surface is MT-146. Provisioning is reconstructable from FR worktree events (TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004).

target_entries: Worktrees > Session branches (session/<id> naming, base ref resolution, detach compat flag HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_DETACH)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Reuse FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CREATED/RECLAIMED with branch/checkout_mode/base_ref/reclaim_policy payload fields; no new kinds.
Emit a diagnostic event on allocation failure (git worktree add non-zero exit) via the open diagnostic-event API if present in the implementing worktree; otherwise record DEFERRED-with-reason.
Short-lived git subprocess; liveness capture surviving a Handshake crash adds no evidence beyond the FR/diagnostic record.

risk_if_missed: Session worktrees stay detached: agent commits are unreachable refs after cleanup, MT-142..147 have no branch to merge, and merge-back is only possible via the lossier patch path.

risks: RISK-1: Branch collision handling silently reuses or force-recreates an existing session/<id> branch, destroying another session's unmerged commits.
RISK-2: The detach compat path drifts (flag ignored or default flipped), breaking every existing caller that assumes detached provisioning and invalidating MT-144's legacy premise.
RISK-3: Branch deletion uses -D (or worktree-style --force) and an unmerged session branch is destroyed on reclaim, losing agent work with no recovery path.

RISK-4: New git invocations skip -c core.longpaths=true or the SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK, producing Windows long-path failures or interleaved `git worktree` metadata corruption under parallel sessions.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Collision path is deterministic suffixing only (-r2..-r99); a live test proves the colliding branch's commits are untouched and no -f/--force reaches `worktree add`/`branch`.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Dedicated compat test asserts the exact legacy command shape (`worktree add --detach <path> HEAD`) when HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_DETACH=1, and default-mode tests never modify pre-existing callers' observable results beyond the added branch.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Deletion is `git branch -d` only; negative test proves an unmerged branch survives a DeleteOnReclaim attempt with a surfaced error; grep proof target asserts no "-D" in branch management code.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Code review + test assert every added Command includes core.longpaths=true and acquires SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK; concurrency test runs two parallel allocations.

research_provenance.source: Verified current code: wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 src/backend/handshake_core/src/workspace_safety.rs (session_worktree_path ~356-368, ensure_session_worktree_allocation ~370-416 `worktree add --detach <path> HEAD` with -c core.longpaths=true under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK, cleanup_session_worktree ~418-440 `worktree remove --force`); swarm_orchestration/events.rs FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CREATED/MOUNTED/RECLAIMED/CLEANUP-FAILED (lines 75-78). Field practice: git worktree add -b is the standard named-branch worktree idiom; `branch -d` fail-closed on unmerged is git's built-in safety and is retained instead of custom merged-state tracking.
corrections: Operator/red-team decisions baked in: never force-push (no push exists in this MT at all); keep-until-merged default branch retention; detach preserved as explicit compat mode, not removed.
Git worktree CODE merge is strictly separated from CRDT document merging (kernel/crdt); boundary stated in scope and forbidden_paths.
